chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the virtue of the beginning of the prayer time over the last is better for a man than his children and his wealth.'

key_terms.الوقت الأخير: The last permissible time for prayer — still valid, but less meritorious
key_terms.الوقت الأول: The beginning/first time of the prayer window — the most meritorious moment to perform salat
key_terms.فضل: Excellence, superiority, virtue — indicating religious merit

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray salat at the beginning or end of the prayer time according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphatically declares that performing the obligatory salat at the very beginning of its prescribed time is superior to performing it at the end of the permitted window — a benefit so great it surpasses even one's children and wealth. This teaching was conveyed through Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi in a chain reaching the Imam, emphasizing the extraordinary spiritual merit that the early adherents of Ahl al-Bayt's school attached to promptness in prayer. For the original audience, comparing a religious act's reward to wealth and offspring — the two greatest worldly goods in Arabian culture — underscored that no worldly consideration should delay salat beyond its preferred time.
